name: Beaver Hall (Residence)
summary: A three-level buff-brick walk-up including a low garden level, where paired balcony stacks with solid end panels break up rows of small windows along the long wings.

evidence.note: The narrow end is largely blank. Long face has three rows, the lowest close to the sidewalk, and paired stacks of balconies with solid end walls. Warm brick sample #b89c7e.
Dark balcony fronts, bright slab edges, groups of small punched openings and a thin dark roof edge.
Eastern elevation has garden-level glazing and alternating paired balconies under a mature canopy.
Glazed common entrance reached from sidewalk between two projecting balcony groups.
Three exposed levels and darker recessed balcony areas, with shallow relief in the brickwork.
Offset bent wings have a continuous pale flat membrane and scattered small vents.
P50 7.8 m, P90 7.9 m, maximum 11.26 m above inventory ground. The broad 7.8–7.9 m plateau fits the two raised living floors above a partly lowered garden level.

notes: Short solid balcony end walls alternate with lighter metal fronts. The grouped-bay settings approximate the paired upper balconies and single-width windows between them. Courtyard doors are estimates. Balcony slabs and solid side cheeks are pale concrete. The front rails are metal pickets. The long Beaver parking face has two adjacent balconies, four ordinary window bays, then two adjacent balconies.
